span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Instructing an observer to respond on a given stimulus dimension makes them exploit whatever conscious information about that dimension exists, which is why a direct task can never be beaten by an indirect one on conscious information.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Apparent direct/indirect dissociations can be manufactured by measuring the two indexes on different stimulus states and displays, so the gap reflects unequal discrimination difficulty rather than unconscious perception.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The empirical conclusion may not generalise beyond the specific display and stimulus parameters used.

span.label: Because the indirect measure was the less sensitive one, the experiments themselves settle nothing about unconscious perception.

span.label: The paper cannot explain why its familiarity/duration correlation runs opposite to Avant's, and leaves that to future work.

span.label: The field's results are stated to be inconclusive because it has no agreed measure of its central term, not because the experiments are poor.
span.note: what this limits: the accumulated literature on perception without awareness: the paper states definitive results have been elusive in the absence of consensus on what constitutes an adequate measure of awareness

span.label: Whether the available measures are even comparable to one another is stated to be unknowable without a framework that does not exist.
span.note: what this limits: comparing results across studies that used different awareness measures: the paper states it is impossible to know whether those measures are adequate or comparable
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The opposing position is rejected on the ground that the thing it depends on cannot be observed.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that a direct discrimination reflects intentional responding: the paper states an observer's intentions cannot be directly observed or measured
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's own diagnosis is that decades of experimental work could not settle the question because the field had no agreed measure of the thing being denied. An empirical programme is stalled by a definitional gap, and the remedy offered is not a better definition but a weaker assumption - an ordering between two sensitivities rather than a claim that either instrument is complete.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

The proposed fix does not settle the definition but MINIMISES what must be assumed - 'THE ONLY ASSUMPTION required by the proposed approach is that the sensitivity of direct discriminations to relevant conscious information is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO' that of comparable indirect ones

span.label: direct measures —operationalised-as→ measure of awareness
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE EXHAUSTIVENESS ASSUMPTION IS MADE. Reading a null on a direct measure as an absence of awareness 'can be true ONLY IF it is also assumed that direct measures provide AN EXHAUSTIVE MEASURE of conscious perceptual experience. Quotation withheld, given conscious perceptual experience' · strength of the relation: 0.9 — A NULL MEASUREMENT MEANS ABSENCE ONLY IF THE INSTRUMENT IS EXHAUSTIVE, and the assumption is usually implicit - the paper calls it 'another IMPLICIT assumption underlying many recent applications of the dissociation paradigm'. This is the 1988 psychology statement of the problem that a verifier cannot report absence.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: indirect measure —distinct-from→ direct measures
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE TWO ARE MEASURED UNDER COMPARABLE CONDITIONS. Avant and Thieman (1985) claimed an indirect measure was MORE sensitive than a direct one; 'CONTRARY TO THIS CLAIM, WHEN DIRECT AND INDIRECT INDEXES ARE MEASURED UNDER COMPARABLE CONDITIONS', the indirect measure is LESS sensitive. The ordering of the two instruments reverses on the comparability of the conditions, not on the instruments · strength of the relation: 0.85 — THE PUBLISHED CLAIM AND ITS REVERSAL USE THE SAME TWO MEASURES. What changed is that they were put on comparable footing - the same lesson as measuring candidates within one run rather than across runs.

span.label: The paper's central deduction is that unconscious perception is established as soon as an indirect measure is absolutely more sensitive to a stimulus dimension than a comparable direct measure.

span.label: Because only relative sensitivity matters, the direct measure no longer has to show zero sensitivity, which removes the null-awareness requirement that had blocked the dissociation paradigm.

span.label: Experiment 1 replicated the filled-duration illusion: displays containing a word or a nonword were judged longer than blank displays of identical physical duration.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: At 50 ms, words were judged longer than nonwords, i.e. familiarity and perceived duration were positively related, the opposite of the negative relation Avant and colleagues report.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The duration-judgment measure is blind to lexical status at 33 ms exposure, showing no word/nonword difference at all.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Lengthening exposure only strengthens the positive familiarity effect rather than reversing its direction.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: With display conditions equated, the direct lexical decision was more sensitive to lexical status than the indirect duration judgment at 33 ms.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same ordering held for stimulus detection in Experiment 4, so on both dimensions the direct measure beat the comparable indirect duration measure and Avant and Thieman's claim was not supported.
